contracts: (For each declared failing Acceptance assertion, captured output orders the matching FAILURE_ID before the failure.) AND (Lifecycle boundary comparison confirms selector, fixture, and assertions are unchanged.) AND (Production diff inspection finds no changed production implementation file outside the declared owner.) AND (RED test execution invokes the declared production owner rather than a substitute.) AND (The RED test structure shows one selector family covering active duplicate, invalid TTL, and non-active release scenarios.) AND (The declared owner provides the bounded stateful ledger behavior under the declared pytest command.) AND (The declared pytest command observes duplicate for the active unexpired claim scenario.) AND (The declared pytest command observes invalid-ttl and no active reservation for the invalid-TTL scenario.) AND (The declared pytest command observes not-found when releasing a non-active key.) AND (The declared test path exists before pytest collection.) AND (Validation uses the exact declared pytest argv.)
selector_intents: Claim an already active unexpired key through the shared ledger selector family.
Claim with non-positive TTL and inspect the resulting ledger state.
Compare established RED selector, fixture, and assertions at GREEN/REFACTOR boundary.
Evaluate whether one RED selector family covers all three required behaviors.
Inspect GREEN production diff paths for the declared owner boundary.
Inspect the declared production owner and execute the shared behavioral selector family.
Observe RED output immediately before each declared failing Acceptance assertion.
Release a non-active key through the shared ledger selector family.
Resolve the declared RED test file path before pytest collection.
Validate using the exact declared pytest argv.
Verify the RED test binds to the declared production owner.
